title: Your Bank Complaints Just Got a Faster, Fairer Fix: Thanks to RBI's New Ombudsman Scheme
description: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has introduced a new and improved system, the Integrated Ombudsman Scheme, 2026 (RB-IOS 2026), to resolve your complaints agai.

faq.q: What kind of complaints can I file under this scheme?
faq.a: You can file complaints about deficiencies in service provided by RBI-regulated entities. This includes issues like failed transactions, unfair charges, mis-selling of products, non-adherence to RBI guidelines, or improper customer service.

faq.q: How long does the Ombudsman take to resolve a complaint?
faq.a: The scheme aims for expeditious resolution. While there isn't a fixed maximum timeline for the Ombudsman's decision, the process is designed to be faster and more efficient than traditional legal routes.

faq.q: Can I appeal if I am not happy with the Ombudsman's decision?
faq.a: Yes, if you are unhappy with an "Award" (decision) passed by the RBI Ombudsman, you can file an appeal with the Appellate Authority within 30 days of receiving the Award.

faq.q: What if my bank or NBFC doesn't follow the Ombudsman's Award?
faq.a: If a regulated entity fails to comply with an Award, the RBI has powers to take action against them, ensuring that the Ombudsman's decisions are enforced.

fact_check.summary: The article provides a largely accurate overview of the RBI's Integrated Ombudsman Scheme, 2026, including its effective date, scope, complaint process, and compensation limits, though some minor details regarding the previous scheme's compensation limit are slightly off.
